title: Tool error (C10)
description: JSON carried in the text content of an MCP tool result with isError: true. One variant per error code; only the fields listed for a code are allowed.

Message.description: Safe text for the user. Never contains backend responses, secrets, argument values or stack traces.

error.description: Only when an administrator disabled the tool or its server, or its definition waits for approval. A tool that the endpoint filter of the request leaves out is not_found_or_denied (CC-118, CC-170).

ConfirmationRequired.description: The confirmation of a destructive call is the current code of the user's TOTP authenticator (C11, CC-091). One of two shapes: a pending call exists (confirmationId, description, previewUrl, expiresAt) or the user has no authenticator and only registerUrl is given.

description.description: Operation as the gateway computed it from the arguments it received: qualified tool name, system and arguments sorted by name, JSON-serialized, truncated like ConfirmationView. Not model text. Unlike message it carries argument values (the client already has them). A client shows it to the user, but a client is untrusted: the portal preview is the reference.

previewUrl.description: Read-only portal page /confirm/<confirmationId> (owner only, a session without fresh MFA is enough). Opening it is optional.

registerUrl.description: Portal page where the user registers the authenticator. Present exactly when the user has no usable authenticator: none registered, or disabled by the daily limit of wrong codes (CC-126); no pending call exists then.

error.description: No pending call, expired, arguments different from the first call, wrong or already used code, or attempts exhausted (C11, CC-091).

connectUrl.description: Portal page where the user connects the account.

error.description: Also the answer for a tool that the endpoint filter of the request leaves out, so that the filter does not reveal which tools exist (CC-118, CC-170, invariant 8), and for a resource that does not exist, that the user may not see or that lies outside the scope granted by policy, including a service desk queue outside the grant (CC-146). The check of the grant comes before the building of any entity, so that no other error reveals the resource.

message.description: One fixed text for every cause (CC-146), so that the text does not tell the causes apart.
message.const: The resource does not exist or you do not have access to it.

error.description: Error of the caller. On a violation of the tool's inputSchema (wrong type, missing or unknown argument, a value outside a bound) the server answers invalid_argument; the message may name an argument declared in the schema and the broken rule, never the value of the argument and never a name that the schema does not declare (CC-078). Text rejected by the text hygiene rules (README, CC-121, CC-122) is invalid_argument too. The text never comes from a backend response.

A tool call over a limit of the gateway (user, user and client, user and tool; CC-156). retryAfterSeconds is at least 1. The settings are never revealed. Requests that are not tool calls get HTTP 429 with the same body shape (test-vectors/gateway-authentication).

stepUpUrl.description: Portal URL that re-authenticates with max_age/acr_values.

error.description: A system, the secret store or the policy source is unavailable. On a server this is also the answer when its policy data is not available (no data after a restart, or the gateway cannot be asked), and the audit reason is policy_unavailable (CC-141).
Also the answer of a server when the credential type in X-MCP-Credential-Type is not one of its accepted types (audit reason credential_type_mismatch, CC-166); the message gives no detail.

The pending call was replaced by a newer DESTRUCTIVE operation of the same user (at most one is pending, CC-127). Answer to the retry of the older call; the code is not checked and no attempt is spent. The user starts the operation again.

Another DESTRUCTIVE operation of this user is waiting for confirmation and its owner has opened the portal preview, so a different DESTRUCTIVE operation is refused until that one is confirmed or the block ends at max(its expiry, preview view + 90 s) (first wins after the preview, CC-127). Nothing was created: a code typed by the user would not confirm this call, so a client MUST NOT ask the user for a code for it; it should say that another operation awaits confirmation and retry later. Without an opened preview the new operation supersedes the old one instead.

The owner cancelled the pending call in the portal (CC-128). Answer to the retry of that call: the code is not checked, no attempt or TOTP step is spent, and a code typed in parallel after the cancel does not confirm it. The user starts the operation again if they still want it.
